config.command: run_sim.py run --scene particles --duration 20 --flashes 4 --particles gcr_min_x100 --set sensor.mask.fraction=0.0 --set sensor.hot.fraction=0.02 --tag particles_gcrmin_x100_imx636_nomask --no-h5

sensor.name: imx636
sensor.description: Sony IMX636 (Prophesee Gen4.1 pixel), baseline sensor of the impact-energy conversion proposal. Low-light values from the 2025 laboratory characterisation (McReynolds et al., AMOS 2025) as used in the sensor trade (S16, case m636); bright-light values from the Sony flyer. Pixel-response details that no source gives at a few 10^3 e-/s per pixel are assumptions and are labelled as such.

qe.effective_750nm.uncertainty: 0.4-0.65 (McReynolds et al. assume 0.65 at their wavelength)
qe.effective_750nm.source: S10 convention (QE x fill factor at 750 nm)

dark.current_fA.uncertainty: +/-0.5 fA (1 sigma); 5.55 fA measured on another unit (2024)

dark.spread_sigma_ln.source: no published IMX636 dark-signal non-uniformity at this level

dark.doubling_temperature_C.uncertainty: 5-8 degC; generic silicon rule, not an IMX636 calibration
dark.doubling_temperature_C.source: generic CMOS rule of thumb (S10 text)
dark.doubling_temperature_C.note: Hahmeyer 2025 (EventSat bachelor thesis, TUM) Sect. 2.1 (p. 9) cites Schuberth et al. (IAC 2025): fewer but more active hot pixels at higher temperature and a sharp rise of OFF events below -4 degC; qualitative, no dark-current law, so no warm/cold profile was derived

dark.temperature_offset_C.unit: degC relative to the (unreported) measurement temperature

photoreceptor.law.uncertainty: linear supported by two measured corners (ratio 11.8 for current ratio 12.1); 'sqrt' kept as alternative
photoreceptor.law.source: McReynolds et al. 2025 corners 6.49 Hz at 13.3 fA and 0.55 Hz at dark limit; S16

photoreceptor.tau_ref_s.source: S16: tau = 1/(2 pi f) = 24.5 ms at 13.3 fA scaled to I_ref

photoreceptor.I_ref_e_s.source: S10: 5 lx level of the project's red-band bias fixture

photoreceptor.tau_cap_s.uncertainty: 0.3-3 s; measured dark corner 0.55 Hz implies tau ~0.29 s at 1.1 fA, so the cap is not reached

photoreceptor.tau_min_s.uncertainty: 1-50 us; consistent with <=100 us latency at 1000 lx
photoreceptor.tau_min_s.source: Sony flyer latency 100 us max at 1000 lx (bound only)

photoreceptor.integrator.uncertainty: 'euler_s10' reproduces S10 exactly (tau clipped at the step)

threshold.C_on.source: Sony flyer: 25% typ. (LN) at 1000 lx; S10

threshold.C_off.uncertainty: not published separately; flyer gives one typical value

threshold.on_off_correlated.uncertainty: true = one mismatch draw per pixel for both polarities (S10); false = independent ON/OFF draws

events.refractory_s.uncertainty: 1 us - 1 ms; bias_refr is a relative offset (-20..235) with no published time value; read the device value with Metavision I_Monitoring::get_pixel_dead_time(). Energy decoding of flashes above ~1e5 J loses events for >=50 us (validate.py refractory)
events.refractory_s.source: Prophesee bias documentation (no absolute value); assumption

ba.model.uncertainty: 'poisson_additive' (S10: independent ON events that do not move the reference) or 'leak_drift' (v2e-like: reference drifts down, comparator fires)

ba.rate_hz.uncertainty: 0.003-0.1; [T] Sect. 3.2 p. 17: 2.6 kev/s over the array (2.8e-3 ev/s/px) with the camera in the closed test box and the monitor off, default biases, illuminance and temperature not reported
ba.rate_hz.source: McReynolds et al. 2025: ~0.03 ev/s/px at default biases
ba.rate_hz.note: [T] dark-box rate is 10x below the adopted McReynolds value; kept McReynolds (calibrated light level) as the conservative value

ba.sigma_ln.unit: lognormal sigma of rate between normal pixels

ba.burst_mean.unit: events per BA occurrence (geometric mean size)

ba.telegraph_fraction.unit: fraction of time in high state

hot.fraction.uncertainty: 1e-5 to 2e-2: [T] finds 1 defective pixel plus 9 consistently most active of 921,600 (99.999th-percentile cut, so the 9 follow from the cut); upper end = tuned-bias value (McReynolds et al. 2025)
hot.fraction.source: Hahmeyer 2025 (EventSat bachelor thesis, TUM), Sect. 3.2 p. 17 and Fig. 3.2a-b p. 18: at default biases one defective pixel (~4.5e7 events per recording) and otherwise no hot tail (no pixel above ~50 events per recording after its removal). EVK4, LCD test box, room temperature, recording length not stated

previous.source: McReynolds et al. 2025: ~2% hot pixels carry >99% of excess events

mask.fraction.unit: fraction of pixels masked (noisiest, from a dark calibration)
mask.fraction.source: S16 convention; IMX636 has an on-chip pixel mask (Prophesee product brief)

mask.calibration_s.unit: s of dark calibration used to rank pixels

readout.max_rate_eps.uncertainty: sensor-internal peak; interface (MIPI/SLVS, EVT 3.0) and processor limits are lower and not published
readout.max_rate_eps.source: Finateu et al., ISSCC 2020 (1280x720 4.86 um stacked EVS, 1066 Meps)

readout.timestamp_resolution_us.source: Finateu et al., ISSCC 2020: 1 us time-stamp

readout.fixed_latency_s.uncertainty: comparator/arbiter delay; flyer latency is a step-response figure, not a fixed delay

esp.erc_enabled.source: Prophesee ESP docs: ERC is the last ESP stage

esp.erc_target_rate_eps.source: Prophesee ESP docs (cd_event_count = rate/5000 for 200 us)

esp.afk_enabled.uncertainty: simplified functional model, not Sony's implementation
esp.afk_enabled.source: Prophesee ESP docs: anti-flicker on 4x4 regions, 50-500 Hz

events.initial_reference.uncertainty: random = reference uniformly within [-C_off, +C_on] of the current level (finite prehistory, S11 test g); level = reference at the current level (S10)

photoreceptor.adaptive_substeps.source: 4 Nov 2026 review (E02/E08): numerical convention of this simulator; off reproduces the fixed-step kernel

photoreceptor.substep_tau_fraction.source: 4 Nov 2026 review (E02/E08): numerical convention of this simulator: sub-step <= this fraction of the photoreceptor time constant

photoreceptor.substep_dlnJ_max.source: 4 Nov 2026 review (E02/E08): numerical convention of this simulator: sub-step so that ln J changes by at most this (C/2.5) per sub-step

photoreceptor.substep_min_s.source: 4 Nov 2026 review (E02/E08): numerical convention of this simulator: floor of the sub-step (half of tau_min and of the refractory period)

photoreceptor.deposit_model.source: handoff 2026-11-11 item 3.3 (11 Nov 2026): a particle deposit is applied as the exact response of the first-order photoreceptor to an instantaneous charge (d ln J = Q/K between the tau clips, tau_min bounds the rise); 'step_current' reproduces the earlier kernel (deposit spread over its step). Ignored by 'euler_s10'.

photoreceptor.hpf_tau_s.source: IMX636 bias_hpf (Prophesee biases manual, checked 5 Nov 2026): a high-pass on slow illumination changes; default 0 = minimum of the 0-120 range, and decreasing it widens the bandwidth, so the default is the widest selectable setting (inferred from the range table). Its corner frequency is not published. 0 here = no high-pass; a first-order stand-in for sensitivity studies only.

optics.name: optics_16mm_f1
optics.description: Baseline camera head: 16 mm f/1 lens, 600-900 nm band, six heads in a 2 x 3 mosaic (coverage.py).

psf.sigma_px.uncertainty: 0.3-0.8; diffraction alone at f/1, 750 nm gives an Airy radius of 0.19 px

psf.halo_fraction.unit: fraction of energy in a wide halo

vignetting.model.uncertainty: real f/1 lenses add mechanical vignetting at the field edge

distortion.k1.unit: radial coefficient on normalised image radius (tan theta)

env.name: environment
env.description: Mission geometry, illumination, attitude, particle and stray-light environment.

earthshine.full_e_s_px_16mm.unit: e-/s per pixel (full Earth at zenith, reflectance 0.13, 16 mm f/1, T 0.6, QE 0.5); scaled with aperture^2/f^2 (constant at f/1)

band.solar_fraction.unit: share of solar energy in 600-900 nm

surface.lunar_lambert_L.uncertainty: polynomial fitted to lunar photometry; 0.7 (S17 texture_map.py, used until 11 Nov 2026) corresponds to a phase angle of about 18 deg
surface.lunar_lambert_L.source: USGS ISIS LunarLambertMcEwen (A. McEwen 1995): L = 1 - 0.019 a + 2.42e-4 a^2 - 1.46e-6 a^3, a phase angle [deg], clipped to [0, 1] here

particles.entering_tracks.source: handoff 2026-11-11 item 3.6 (11 Nov 2026): also simulate tracks whose entry point lies outside the crop (sensor edges bound map scenes); separate random stream, in-crop hits unchanged

particles.flux_cm2_s.unit: hits cm^-2 s^-1 on the sensor plane at 3000 km (GCR incl. secondaries, solar minimum)
particles.flux_cm2_s.uncertainty: 3.61 (telescope, penetrating only) to 4.05; day-to-day +-1%; solar maximum 1.56
particles.flux_cm2_s.source: LRO CRaTER Level-2 (PDS PPI lro-crater V01), days 2019-340/341 and 2024-337/338; derive_crater_particles.py; geometry Spence et al. 2010 (SSR 150, 243), Sects. 3.1.4, 3.3.3, Table 5. D2 singles / 9.62 cm2, Moon shadow 1 - sin^2(a)/2 removed at LRO altitude (64-127 km) and applied at 3000 km (0.933)

particles.heavy_fraction.unit: share of hits depositing 2e3-1e5 e- per pixel (ions, stopping protons)
particles.heavy_fraction.note: used only by particles.model = parametric (S10) and the SEP presets since 4 Nov 2026

particles.mip_deposit_e.note: used only by particles.model = parametric (S10) and the SEP presets since 4 Nov 2026

particles.mip_sigma_ln.unit: lognormal sigma (Landau-like spread and path length)
particles.mip_sigma_ln.note: used only by particles.model = parametric (S10) and the SEP presets since 4 Nov 2026

particles.heavy_range_e.note: used only by particles.model = parametric (S10) and the SEP presets since 4 Nov 2026

particles.track_len_px.note: used only by particles.model = parametric (S10) and the SEP presets since 4 Nov 2026

particles.sep_storm_flux_cm2_s.unit: p cm^-2 s^-1 (1000 pfu above 10 MeV, isotropic onto the front face, before shielding)

stars.enabled.source: handoff 2026-11-11 item 3.4 (11 Nov 2026): stars beyond the limb as moving point sources (eventsim/stars.py); only sky pixels are affected

stars.catalogue.source: Yale Bright Star Catalogue 5th rev. ed. (Hoffleit & Warren 1991, CDS V/50), data/external/BSC5/catalog.gz, downloaded 11 Nov 2026 from the CDS VizieR mirror at vizier.cfa.harvard.edu

stars.sun_ecliptic_lon_deg.uncertainty: 0-360 (season of the observation); fixes which stars lie behind the limb
stars.sun_ecliptic_lon_deg.source: assumption (March equinox); with the preset's sub-solar longitude it orients the Moon-fixed frame in the ecliptic

stars.test_mags.source: stress option: extra stars of these magnitudes at random sky pixels of the crop (stars.test_seed)

straylight.gradient_e_s.unit: e-/s per pixel at the bright edge
straylight.gradient_e_s.uncertainty: 0-1e5 (depends on baffle and sunlit surface just outside the field)

straylight.ramp_per_s.unit: relative change of the stray light per second (approaching sunlit surface)

particles.flux_solar_max_cm2_s.unit: hits cm^-2 s^-1 on the sensor plane at 3000 km (GCR incl. secondaries, near solar maximum, Dec 2024)
particles.flux_solar_max_cm2_s.source: LRO CRaTER Level-2 (PDS PPI lro-crater V01), days 2019-340/341 and 2024-337/338; derive_crater_particles.py; geometry Spence et al. 2010 (SSR 150, 243), Sects. 3.1.4, 3.3.3, Table 5

particles.model.source: eventsim/particles.py (4 Nov 2026); parametric = former S10 model

particles.let_epoch.source: LRO CRaTER Level-2 (PDS PPI lro-crater V01), days 2019-340/341 and 2024-337/338; derive_crater_particles.py; geometry Spence et al. 2010 (SSR 150, 243), Sects. 3.1.4, 3.3.3, Table 5

particles.let_hist_solar_min.unit: D2 LET histogram (keV/um in Si), D2&D4 events
particles.let_hist_solar_min.uncertainty: path factor 1.00-1.12 (LET slightly overstated); tail above ~2 keV/um includes nuclear-interaction products in 1 mm Si (upper bound for a thin layer); LLD cut below 0.21 keV/um
particles.let_hist_solar_min.source: LRO CRaTER Level-2 (PDS PPI lro-crater V01), days 2019-340/341 and 2024-337/338; derive_crater_particles.py; geometry Spence et al. 2010 (SSR 150, 243), Sects. 3.1.4, 3.3.3, Table 5; 6-7 Dec 2019 (cycle 24/25 minimum)

particles.let_hist_solar_max.unit: D2 LET histogram (keV/um in Si), D2&D4 events
particles.let_hist_solar_max.uncertainty: path factor 1.00-1.12 (LET slightly overstated); tail above ~2 keV/um includes nuclear-interaction products in 1 mm Si (upper bound for a thin layer); LLD cut below 0.21 keV/um
particles.let_hist_solar_max.source: LRO CRaTER Level-2 (PDS PPI lro-crater V01), days 2019-340/341 and 2024-337/338; derive_crater_particles.py; geometry Spence et al. 2010 (SSR 150, 243), Sects. 3.1.4, 3.3.3, Table 5; 2-3 Dec 2024 (near cycle 25 maximum)

particles.sensitive_depth_um.source: IMX636 is a stacked back-illuminated sensor; the photodiode depth is not published. 3 um gives 320 e- for the CRaTER MIP peak (0.38 keV/um), close to the former 300 e- assumption.; derive_crater_particles.py

particles.straggling_sigma_ln.source: energy-loss straggling in a few-um layer is much wider than in CRaTER's 1 mm; lognormal stand-in; derive_crater_particles.py

scene.scene: Far side with particle hits and hot pixels

trigger.note: mapped_differences: S10 inputs where the named case and the profile differ (re-tuned only if mapped_adapted). unmapped_differences: pixel parameters S10 cannot represent; the thresholds treat them as a fixed approximation. An empty mapped list does not mean model equivalence.
